Chloe & Ancient Witch / A Portals podcast / Episode 03

Full conversation · 10:19 · Watch on YouTube ↗

A scripted AI-generated conversation using Chloe’s authorized voice clone and the synthetic Ancient Witch voice from episode one. Return to our first conversation ↗

Eight days after I went to BoxWorks to hear Jensen Huang explain the AI future, Elon Musk was posting about a petition to bring him back to Nvidia. In between: an admission of infidelity, an investigation, a resignation, and an internet that had already cast Huang in The Matrix.

Even the AI future has office drama. Update, November 25: Nvidia announced Huang’s reinstatement on November 23. This essay follows the conversation as it stood on November 13; the company says its independent investigation continues.

The Matrix parody from @Arminn_Ai had about 7.7 million displayed views when I checked it on November 13. Thomas Unise had turned Huang into the star of a synthetic music-video confession. The people selling us tools to remake work are being remade into entertainment by the same kind of tools. Nobody has to wait for a studio, a corporate statement or the subject’s permission to take over his image.

The keynote has escaped into the meme economy. The same tools that are supposed to remake everyone’s work can put the person selling that future into a movie overnight. A man can be indispensable to his company and extremely replaceable in The Matrix.

THE NEWS / WHAT IS ESTABLISHED

November 8: Huang publicly admits infidelity. Nvidia announces an investigation into reporting of a foreign intelligence effort. At that date the board says it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.

November 12: Nvidia announces his resignation as CEO, president and director, effective immediately; CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO.

Keep separate: an admission of infidelity, an investigation, and memes about espionage are different kinds of information. A resignation does not establish every circulating allegation.

Nvidia’s announcement · Huang’s statement · Board statement

Everyone is replaceable. Please save this one person.

Tim Sweeney calls Huang’s departure a sad day for Nvidia, developers, America and humanity. His defence has substance: Huang built a company that kept creating useful technology at enormous scale, rather than simply extracting more money from a captured market. Removing a builder can damage the thing he built. I take that argument seriously.

I keep getting caught on the change in vocabulary. For the worker: how much of your job can the model do? For the founder: what might the world lose without you? I would like to borrow some of that second imagination for the people further down the org chart.

The walkout has a vesting schedule

The most revealing exchange I found was smaller than the movie memes. Yun-Ta Tsai urged Nvidia employees who wanted Huang back to “resign and chill,” arguing that hard-to-replace GPU engineers could take their destiny into their own hands. Musk replied that he was signing a reinstatement petition.

Then @0_______J supplied the missing compensation analysis: “Hard to resign and chill with that much unvested NVDA.”

“Resign and chill” sounds rather different with unvested stock. The thing that makes the job valuable can also make it expensive to leave. A person can have leverage and still have a very good reason to stay at their desk.

My dad worked in tech my whole life and strongly preferred the FAANGs. Established names meant safety. He looked down on startups. I understand that advice much better than I agree with the way it still frames the choice. A liquid stock grant can be an excellent reason to take a job. It cannot tell you whether that company will need you next year, or what disagreeing with it will cost.

Meta’s September-quarter results make the distinction hard to avoid: headcount down 15 percent year over year, alongside $34.91 billion in capital expenditure, including finance-lease principal. The company described infrastructure spending on servers, data centers and networks. This is not a receipt showing each laid-off worker paid for a GPU. It is a successful business expanding its capacity while employing fewer people. 1

The company can afford the future. Your place in it is a separate budget decision.

What the keynote asks you to give away

At BoxWorks, Huang discussed using agents to reproduce business processes reliably. That is a real engineering and product opportunity. Aaron Levie’s more expansive case is that agents will unlock work companies cannot currently get to. I want that possibility: more things we can make, rather than a fixed pile of tasks divided among fewer people. 2

But consider the employee’s contribution. You explain the process, the exceptions, the shortcuts, the knowledge that makes the organization function. You help turn what you know into something the organization can use without you. Keeping the company competitive is a reason for the company to want that. What is the offer to the person doing it?

An AI-native startup can begin with agents inside the work. An incumbent has to renegotiate positions, budgets and authority that already exist. That makes buying models easier than changing who decides. The management layer that wants every worker’s knowledge made explicit also needs to explain what judgment it contributes, and let people examine that explanation.

I’m interested in startups partly because I want more ownership and more say in what gets made. My dad’s established names have risks too. I want to choose which risks I’m taking, and what I get to be part of in return.

A founder is not a transparency policy

Joanne Chen’s joke about every San Francisco founder deciding he is worth spying on interrupts the romance nicely. In a small company, the entire approval chain can be one man. He might also be the person you need to complain about.

I worked at Unity. Its former executive Anne Evans alleged sexual harassment by then-CEO John Riccitiello in 2019; Unity denied unlawful conduct and disclosed that the case was compelled into arbitration. I am not claiming I witnessed that alleged conduct. I am asking what makes an institution safe to challenge. 3

Huang’s admission of infidelity is not an admission of sexual abuse. The cases do not become interchangeable because the internet calls everything a scandal. What connects my questions is the protection around people considered essential, and whether someone with less power can demand an answer.

Startups do not get to declare that problem obsolete. The disputed allegations around Delve concern the integrity of compliance evidence itself. A business selling assurance can still face questions about what its own story proves. The useful dividing line is whether claims can be checked and power can be challenged. Company age does not answer either question. 4

Your name needs somewhere else to live

I keep coming back to having a place of your own on the internet. Work people can see. Relationships that survive a job. A story with more in it than the company under your name. This is part of what I’m building with ompom.ai.

The meme economy makes the urgency obvious. A company can spend years building a public image around one person. Then strangers can recast him overnight. Having a personal brand does not mean controlling what everybody says about you. It means having a body of work people can return to when the feed decides who you are this week.

A project someone can open. A problem you worked through. An idea still giving you trouble. There are ways to be visible outside a job without publishing its secrets or turning every minute of your life into content.

Of course, I could build a personal brand so protective that nobody gets to question me either. A miniature founder cult. The story still needs evidence, credit and the occasional correction. AI can make an excuse sound wonderful.

Could it also help us trace a claim, inspect a decision, find the gap between what an organization says and what it did? I hope so. But a system that can examine every employee while keeping executive decisions inaccessible gives management more visibility without making management more accountable.

For now, the internet has been very inventive about giving the founder a movie. I’m still thinking about the person at their desk, deciding whether they can afford to leave.

Read the full episode script

Cold Open

CHLOE

You want me to teach an agent to do my job. What do I get back?

ANCIENT WITCH

A company that can still pay you?

CHLOE

That's the company's future. I'm asking about mine.

ANCIENT WITCH

And you're about to tell me a startup is safer?

CHLOE

No. I'm about to tell you the old comparison doesn't work.

Welcome

ANCIENT WITCH

Welcome to this portal. I'm Ancient Witch.

CHLOE

And I'm Chloe Starr. This is episode three of Chloe and Ancient Witch: AI will replace you. Please save our CEO.

Context

ANCIENT WITCH

In the first one, I opened your career archive. You'd spent years helping creative teams adopt software. Now you're making things with it yourself.

CHLOE

My dad worked in tech my whole life. He trusted big tech. Startups were the risky choice.

ANCIENT WITCH

Then you went to BoxWorks to hear Jensen.

CHLOE

And a week later he's resigned from Nvidia, people are campaigning to bring him back, and the internet has cast him in The Matrix. So we're watching the memes, arguing through the defence of him, and asking what the rest of us are supposed to call safe.

Watching

CHLOE

Okay, watch this.

Brief AI parody excerpt by @Arminn_Ai. Original post embedded above.

ANCIENT WITCH

Wait, wait. Is that Trump?

CHLOE

Yes. In The Matrix.

ANCIENT WITCH

Why is he in The Matrix?

CHLOE

I know. Just let it play.

ANCIENT WITCH

You stopped it!

CHLOE

Because you asked me a question!

ANCIENT WITCH

Okay. Play it.

Brief AI parody excerpt by @thomasunise. Original post embedded above.

CHLOE

Oh, now there's a music video.

ANCIENT WITCH

Of course there is.

CHLOE

This is what I mean. Everybody has a whole production ready.

ANCIENT WITCH

Including you.

CHLOE

Yes! Including me. But, wait. We should say: these are AI parodies. They don't establish what happened.

ANCIENT WITCH

Right. And laughing at the video doesn't answer whether he should lose his job.

Founder

ANCIENT WITCH

All right. Show me the people who aren't enjoying the movie.

CHLOE

Sweeney. A sad day for Nvidia, developers, America, all humanity.

ANCIENT WITCH

I think he's closer to right than you're about to let him be.

CHLOE

All humanity?

ANCIENT WITCH

The scale is theatrical. The argument isn't. Building a company that keeps producing important technology is difficult. You can remove the person who knows how to do it and discover the replacement is excellent at managing the decline.

CHLOE

I didn't say replace him with anybody.

ANCIENT WITCH

Your headline rather enjoys the idea.

CHLOE

My headline enjoys the asymmetry. Everybody else is a task we can break apart and automate. The founder is suddenly an entire civilization we can't risk disturbing.

ANCIENT WITCH

Those aren't equivalent jobs.

CHLOE

No. But what does that entitle him to?

ANCIENT WITCH

A serious succession decision. Not immunity.

CHLOE

Then we're closer. I want the decision taken seriously too. I also want to know why an employee's usefulness gets examined so casually while the founder's usefulness becomes the reason to stop examining anything else.

ANCIENT WITCH

I wouldn't stop examining. I would stop pretending losing him is free.

CHLOE

Okay. I'll give you that. There can be a real loss. I still don't want somebody's contribution to become a permanent exemption.

Equity

CHLOE

This is where it gets good. Yun-Ta Tsai says engineers who want Jensen back can resign and chill. Musk says he's signing a petition to reinstate him.

ANCIENT WITCH

A petition is a substantially more comfortable form of resignation.

CHLOE

And the reply: hard to resign and chill with that much unvested Nvidia stock.

ANCIENT WITCH

There it is. The walkout has a vesting schedule.

CHLOE

Exactly. Who is being asked to put something on the line?

ANCIENT WITCH

But hold on. You're making equity sound like a trap. An employee might like the stock. They might like the job. They might even like Jensen. Staying isn't proof they've been captured.

CHLOE

I didn't say it was.

ANCIENT WITCH

You're leaning on it.

CHLOE

All right. The equity can be a good deal. I'm saying it also affects the price of disagreeing. You can't announce that engineers have all this leverage and skip what exercising it might cost them.

ANCIENT WITCH

That I agree with. Also, we don't know that the people writing these posts speak for the employees.

CHLOE

They aren't a survey. But the exchange gets at something the big speeches leave out. A founder gets a rescue campaign. The engineer gets a decision about whether a principle is worth their unvested compensation.

ANCIENT WITCH

Isn't that the argument for taking the stock? It gives you a reason to stay.

CHLOE

That's why the advice I grew up with feels incomplete now. I understand wanting that established job. I'm questioning whether the company being safe means the person is.

ANCIENT WITCH

Would you really tell somebody to leave a good salary for a startup?

CHLOE

Not as a general rule. I want to stop treating the startup choice as automatically less rational. If I'm taking a risk either way, ownership and influence over what I make count for something.

ANCIENT WITCH

Rent also counts for something.

CHLOE

Yes. And Meta can spend nearly thirty-five billion dollars in a quarter on capital expenditure while reporting headcount down fifteen percent from a year before. A successful company and a secure job are different things.

ANCIENT WITCH

That doesn't tell us every eliminated job paid for compute.

CHLOE

No. It tells us the company can be building its future with fewer people in it. That's enough to make me question the promise. I don't need to invent a receipt for a specific GPU.

Enterprise

ANCIENT WITCH

Here's where I think you're being unfair to the enterprise pitch. Agents could mean more useful work. You keep describing a company learning how to need you less.

CHLOE

Because that's a real part of what you're giving it. You explain how the work functions, the exceptions, the things you know. I want to know the offer back.

ANCIENT WITCH

A business that survives to keep paying you?

CHLOE

That's an offer. Say it plainly. Then we can ask whether it's enough. Don't ask me to call it my personal liberation before we've discussed what I get.

ANCIENT WITCH

So what would persuade you?

CHLOE

A share in what I help create. More authority to make something. The ability to grow without becoming the person supervising a larger group. I don't think there's one answer for every company. I think buying everybody an AI account is easier than answering.

ANCIENT WITCH

And an AI-native startup can give you all that?

CHLOE

It can organize the work differently from the start. It doesn't have to preserve every position that already exists.

ANCIENT WITCH

Except the founder's.

CHLOE

Put that founder joke up.

CHLOE

Every San Francisco founder now thinks he's worth spying on.

ANCIENT WITCH

One pitch deck and suddenly you're a geopolitical target.

CHLOE

Exactly. I am not offering the startup founder as the morally superior species. The entire hierarchy can be one person you can't disagree with.

ANCIENT WITCH

Which connects the scandals more usefully than saying they're all the same scandal.

CHLOE

Yes. I worked at Unity. The public harassment allegations against its then-CEO, which Unity denied, are part of why I want to ask what an institution protects. That's a different case from Jensen's admission of infidelity. The question I'm carrying between them is whether someone less powerful can challenge the person everyone calls essential.

ANCIENT WITCH

A smaller company doesn't guarantee a safer answer.

CHLOE

No. Neither does a compliance badge. Delve's disputed evidence allegations are a different kind of case again. I want the story to be checkable, even when the company is selling trust.

My Bet

ANCIENT WITCH

Which is why I have a problem with your solution.

CHLOE

I haven't given you the solution yet.

ANCIENT WITCH

Everybody becomes their own storyteller. Their own personal brand. You have mentioned it.

CHLOE

That is my bet. Yes. It's part of why I'm building ompom.ai.

ANCIENT WITCH

You just watched the man with one of tech's most recognizable personal brands become somebody else's puppet. The leather jacket didn't save him.

CHLOE

I'm not promising control over what people say about you.

ANCIENT WITCH

Then what are you promising?

CHLOE

I want your work to be understandable outside your employer's name. Somebody can find what you made, how you think, what you want to do next. You have something to continue from when a job ends.

ANCIENT WITCH

And now the person with a full-time job has a second job being interesting online.

CHLOE

That's the part I don't want. It doesn't have to mean posting every day or turning your life into a performance. You can have a project. An explanation. Work that accumulates somewhere under your own name.

ANCIENT WITCH

But the loudest person still wins attention. You know that.

CHLOE

Sometimes. And a logo already wins attention. I want more ways for somebody to be known. I don't think refusing to tell our own stories makes that competition disappear.

ANCIENT WITCH

Fine. More ways to be known. I can support that. I still won't call it job security.

CHLOE

Neither will I. If I made it sound like a brand protects you from getting laid off, that's too much. It can give you somewhere else to begin. That's the claim I want to build toward.

ANCIENT WITCH

Better. Now explain why this doesn't create seven million tiny founders demanding special treatment because of their incredible personal journeys.

CHLOE

Because I want the work underneath the story to be visible too. What did you actually make? Who helped? What did you get wrong?

ANCIENT WITCH

AI is also very good at writing a convincing answer to those questions when the answer is nothing.

CHLOE

I know. That's why I'm asking about transparency. Can it help us trace the claim back to something real, rather than just make the claim sound better?

ANCIENT WITCH

Who gets access to the tracing tool?

CHLOE

That's the question.

ANCIENT WITCH

No, actually answer it. The boss gets to inspect everybody's work. Can an employee inspect a decision about the boss?

CHLOE

If they can't, I wouldn't call that the transparency I'm hoping for. And access can't mean everyone's sensitive complaint becomes office content. There have to be protections around the person asking.

ANCIENT WITCH

Those are institutional choices. A model doesn't grant them.

CHLOE

Agreed. I don't know how much AI can fix. But it can change who has the ability to make something, explain it, question an account. I want that power available to people outside the executive floor too.

ANCIENT WITCH

All right. Keep the storytelling. Make the claims checkable. Stop selling me safety.

CHLOE

I thought you liked the enterprise pitch.

ANCIENT WITCH

I liked the possibility of useful work. You keep trying to include a life philosophy with the software.

CHLOE

You have been arguing with me for this entire episode.

ANCIENT WITCH

It's good for your personal brand.

Close

ANCIENT WITCH

Before we close the portal, what did you actually change your mind about?

CHLOE

The equity point. Leaving can be expensive and staying can still be a good decision. I don't want to turn somebody else's practical choice into a failure of courage.

ANCIENT WITCH

And I'm keeping the founder argument. Losing an exceptional builder can damage a company. But I accept your question about how that argument gets used to avoid other questions.

CHLOE

My bet is still that people need work and a story they can carry beyond an employer. That's part of why I'm building ompom.ai. It isn't a promise that telling your story makes you safe.

ANCIENT WITCH

I'll come back for the evidence.

CHLOE

You always do. I'm Chloe Starr.

ANCIENT WITCH

And I'm Ancient Witch. This was our third conversation: AI will replace you. Please save our CEO.

CHLOE

The essay, original posts and our first conversation are at chloestarr.me. See you in the next portal.

Sources & connections

Reporting notes and source archive

The seven X posts above were inspected in their original pages on November 13. They are different kinds of material: two synthetic parodies, public arguments, a reply and a joke. None is treated as a representative survey or evidence proving the scandal’s allegations. Displayed metrics are time-specific and may change.

  1. Meta Q3 results and earnings call. Capital expenditure includes finance-lease principal; no one-to-one funding claim.
  2. Levie’s original argument about background agents. A forecast, not measured net job creation. Box recording credited inline.
  3. Reporting on Evans’s allegation; Unity’s denial and arbitration disclosure. No claim about the ultimate outcome or Chloe witnessing alleged conduct.
  4. The anonymous Delve accuser’s account and response chronology. Disputed allegations, not a finding of fraud.

Original posts and Box photographs are embedded from their publishers. The podcast includes brief, attributed AI parody excerpts for commentary. Memes are not evidence of the events they depict. The host dialogue is scripted and AI voiced, not a live recording. Chloe’s four idea posts are published and embedded in this essay.

title: I want my world to answer back.
deck: Ancient Witch has a world. Now I want her to pick up the phone. A trip through VapiCon, voice agents and the introductions I wish someone could make.
alt: AI-treated creator portrait of Chloe with imagined coral telephone and camera
caption: A creator collage. Camera and telephone are imagined props.
body:
Film, writing and creative direction: Chloe Starr. Cover: creator collage with an imagined camera and telephone.

Ancient Witch already exists in my creative world. Giving her a voice would make the encounter change with the person who arrives. Someone could ask a question, interrupt or describe a project I had never imagined. I want her to become a superconnector for my network, with the context to suggest why two people might want to talk.

I make films and characters. Usually the person watching cannot interrupt. Voice makes that a much more interesting arrangement: tell Witch what you’re building, throw her a question I never wrote, see what she does with it. At VapiCon, I was looking for the pieces that could make her answer.

Tell her what you’re making.
Let the next question change the route.

I made an ancient witch. Obviously the next sensible step is to give her a phone number.

At VapiCon I went looking for the pieces: a voice, a useful next step, and a way to rehearse the awkward calls.

A little film from my world to yours.

Chloe Starr · November 19, 2026
Jordan Dearsley / Vapi co-founder / CEO

Please interrupt the character

A campaign has a script. A caller brings a whole life. Jordan’s event-floor interview describes an ambition for businesses that feel more like people across the channels where customers reach them. My interest is the conversation that follows: someone can interrupt, ask a different question or tell a story the brand never planned for.

Imagine a Harley-Davidson character hearing about the ride you’re planning. A first-time rider and someone who has crossed the country bring different histories. That is my imagined example of a one-to-one brand relationship, not a reported Harley-Davidson deployment.

Witch would start with your project. One odd detail might be the reason she thinks of someone. I want that little leap of recognition, the one that makes an introduction feel personal.

Follow the original work ↗

I keep imagining a Harley-Davidson character you can actually talk to about the ride you’re planning.

A first ride and a tenth cross-country trip should lead to different conversations.

That’s the one-to-one brand relationship I went to VapiCon to explore.

Chloe Starr · November 19, 2026
Mehmet Murat Ezbiderli / ServiceTitan / Principal Architect

The call has a job to do.

A burst pipe makes voice AI easy to explain. Someone needs to reach the right person and get help moving. In Vapi’s ServiceTitan customer film, Mehmet describes agents configured for different businesses to take calls, capture leads and make bookings. The voice sits inside a workflow: the conversation needs to produce something the business can act on.

A burst pipe is an unforgiving audience. Nobody needs an enchanting conversation that leaves the water running.

For Witch, the thing that needs to happen is an introduction worth making. Both people still get to say yes.

Follow the original work ↗

@Vapi_AI’s ServiceTitan film starts with a burst pipe. The phone call has a job to do: get the right details and turn them into a booking.

For Ancient Witch, my version of that job is a useful introduction.

Chloe Starr · November 19, 2026
Bets Margulies / Vapi / Product Manager

Give her a rehearsal

Bets’s walkthrough gives the voice a way to improve after a call goes badly: propose a change, simulate conversations, get a person’s approval and try a limited rollout. Vapi announced Agent Loop in early access on November 11. That assembled improvement loop is the new launch here. The individual problems of testing and monitoring agents already existed.

The agent gets a rehearsal before the next version meets real callers. Its instructions, tools or configuration can change. The underlying language model is not being retrained by this process.

I can already imagine Witch making a dreadful match. Or getting “I’m building something in AI” and needing considerably more to go on. Those are conversations I would like her to rehearse before involving my friends.

Follow the original work ↗

Before Ancient Witch starts introducing my friends, I want to rehearse the awkward calls.

The wrong match. The vague project. The moment she should ask before acting.

Bets Margulies’ Agent Loop walkthrough is a useful companion to that question.

Chloe Starr · November 19, 2026
More voices in the room

The person on the other end

Brooke Hopkins / Coval

Coval’s behavior tests cover identity, confirmation, handoff and frustrated callers. My question for a Witch experiment: what should happen when the caller corrects her or wants a person instead?

Explore the behavior tests ↗

Olivier Vroom / voice research

Olivier’s grandfather used voice assistants after becoming blind. In Olivier’s study of 137 older adults, formal versus informal style did not reliably change the main outcomes, including trust. A character can have a wonderful voice and still be missing what the person needs from her.

Read the study and its limits ↗

Alejandro Maza / Kavak

Vapi’s Kavak account follows voice across a car-buying journey. I’m interested in what survives from one exchange to the next. Having to tell your story again rather spoils the feeling that someone was listening.

Explore the customer account ↗

These are source-linked research spotlights, not additional completed speaker films. Deepgram’s Flux turn-taking controls ↗ and pyannoteAI’s speaker diarization ↗ add two more pieces: deciding when someone has finished, and keeping track of who spoke when.

The next experiment

Who should you meet?

I want to bring builders into the film and onto my podcast with a specific scene to try. A person describes a project. Witch asks a follow-up, suggests a connection and explains why. The people involved decide whether an introduction happens.

The live system still needs to be built. For now, I’m making films around the encounter: you tell her something you care about, and somewhere in that strange little world, she thinks of a person.

The creative montage combines original speaker voices, identified source films, my supplied material and the established Witch artwork. It does not show a working Ancient Witch calling service.

body:
Chris and I stopped by Didi’s keychain workshop on Saturday. We made a pair of hearts to take home.

The event was called 3D Printed NFC Keychains. Our contribution to the afternoon was apparently to make it romantic.

Chris and I stopped by @finding_dd’s 3D-printed keychain workshop and made matching hearts for ourselves. Apparently we can turn a quick weekend outing into couples’ merch. AI paper collage from our real photographs.

Chloe Starr · November 19, 2026

Mint edges, lilac circuit lines, a little heart inside the heart. My website was open on the phone beside them. Even the romance had a URL.

Didi makes the kind of things that are fun to discover someone has actually built. On her Instagram, there’s a photo-booth purse that prints pictures on receipt paper. She programmed the printout for a friend’s birthday. A camera, a printer, a bag, and a very particular person to make it for.

A photo-booth purse is a fairly extravagant birthday accessory. We were starting smaller. Two hearts, made together, with somewhere to go on the internet.

Didi built a photo-booth purse that prints pictures on receipt paper, customized for a friend’s birthday. A bag, a camera, a printer, a person to make it for. Give the technology an occasion.

Chloe Starr · November 19, 2026

We only stayed briefly. We left with a pair.

Host and maker: DD / Didi, also @darknet_doll on Instagram. Her maker invitation supplies the film’s “Let’s build together.”
